chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) that he said:
The eating of the crow is not forbidden; rather, the forbidden is only what God has forbidden in His Book, but the souls shy away from much of it out of aversion.
ai.seo_question: Is eating crow meat haram or makruh in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani's chain, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ontological status of crow meat, distinguishing between *haram* (divine prohibition) and *makruh* (disliked due to natural aversion or *tazaqqum*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that unless explicitly stated in the Quran or Sunnah, food items are generally permissible (*mubah*), with aversion being a subjective, natural trait rather than a legal barrier. The narration underscores the reliability of the *Ahl al-Bayt* in delineating between intrinsic divine commands and cultural or biological preferences.
